title: Report on CHIIR 2026 Workshop on Generative AI and Academic Search (GAI&AS)
summary: This report summarizes the CHIIR 2026 Workshop on Generative AI and Academic Search (GAI\&AS), which examined how GenAI is reshaping academic search systems and research practices. The workshop brought together researchers in human information interaction and information retrieval to explore key challenges and opportunities in designing and evaluating future academic search systems that integrate GenAI, moving beyond traditional document retrieval to support summarization, recommendation, synthesis, and conversational interaction. Participants' interests and discussions focused on three thematic clusters: foundations and principles, applications and opportunities, and search-as-learning. Across these themes, the workshop highlighted the importance of academic search systems in supporting transparency, credibility, research integrity, and long-term scholarly needs, as well as in fostering higher-order cognitive processes. Participants discussed guiding theories, design principles, methodological approaches, partnerships, and community-building efforts aimed at advancing human-centered GenAI-enhanced academic search systems. Overall, the workshop demonstrated strong community interest and a diverse range of ongoing and emerging research initiatives at the intersection of GenAI and academic search.

title: Crop Recommendation and Agricultural Query Answering System Using Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks and Hybrid Retrieval Augmentation
summary: This paper presents a unified system designed to support precision agriculture by integrating advanced weather prediction, crop recommendation, and a question-answering tool for farmers. We propose two deep learning models -- a Transformer-based Graph Neural Network and a Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (STGCN) -- to forecast weather conditions for the next 30 days using data from 1,359 locations in Nepal. The STGCN outperforms the Transformer-based model in accuracy (MSE ~0.011 vs. 0.013), effectively modeling both spatial and temporal dependencies in climate data. These predictions are combined with static soil properties such as pH, moisture, and organic content to generate localized crop recommendations through a scoring algorithm that matches each crop's optimal growing conditions. Additionally, we develop a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot that leverages domain-specific agricultural documents to answer farmers' questions in natural language. The entire system is deployed via a mobile application, offering real-time suggestions and conversational support. User feedback confirms the system's usability and relevance, especially in rural settings where personalized farming guidance is limited. Overall, our approach demonstrates how combining machine learning models with local agricultural data can empower farmers with actionable insights, promoting more informed decisions, better crop yields, and increased resilience to climate variability.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个面向精准农业的统一系统，整合了基于时空图神经网络的天气预报、结合土壤数据的作物推荐和基于混合检索增强生成的农业问答聊天机器人，部署为移动应用，经用户反馈验证了可用性。
AI.motivation: 农村地区缺乏个性化农业指导，农民需要可及的、本地化的决策支持来应对气候变异性，提升作物产量，因此需要整合天气预报、作物推荐和农业问答的一体化实用系统。
AI.method: 1. 提出Transformer基图神经网络和时空图卷积网络（STGCN）两种模型，利用尼泊尔1359个地点数据预测未来30天天气；2. 将天气预报结果结合土壤pH、湿度、有机质含量等静态属性，通过匹配作物最优生长条件的评分算法生成本地化作物推荐；3. 开发基于检索增强生成（RAG）的聊天机器人，利用农业领域文档回答农民自然语言问题；4. 整体系统部署为移动应用。
AI.result: STGCN在天气预测上准确率优于Transformer基模型（MSE约为0.011对比0.013），可有效建模气候数据的时空依赖；用户反馈验证了系统在个性化农业指导匮乏的农村环境下具备良好的可用性和相关性。
AI.conclusion: 结合机器学习模型和本地农业数据的方案能够为农民提供可操作的决策洞察，帮助农民做出更明智的决策，提升作物产量，增强农业对气候变异性的韧性，所提出的一体化系统可有效支持精准农业。

title: On Choosing the $μ$ Parameter in Gaussian Differential Privacy
summary: Recent work argues for using Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) to report the privacy guarantees in privacy-preserving machine learning. We provide principled mappings from pure-DP $\varepsilon$ to GDP $μ$ by matching the worst-case success of a strong-adversary membership inference attack in terms of three metrics: multiplicative advantage at fixed FPR, precision at fixed recall, and the standard privacy profile. We tabulate $μ$ values across a useful range of parameters and recommend $μ\approx \varepsilon/5$ as a conservative general-purpose conversion.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the conversion between pure differential privacy (pure-DP) parameter ε and Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) parameter μ, provides principled mappings matched by membership inference attack performance, tabulates useful values, and recommends a general conservative conversion μ≈ε/5.
AI.motivation: Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) is increasingly used to report privacy guarantees for privacy-preserving machine learning, but there is a lack of clear, principled guidance on how to convert the widely used pure-DP ε parameter to the corresponding GDP μ parameter, which creates a gap for practical adoption of GDP.
AI.method: The authors derive mappings from pure-DP ε to GDP μ by matching the worst-case success of a strong-adversary membership inference attack, evaluated on three standard metrics: multiplicative advantage at fixed false positive rate (FPR), precision at fixed recall, and the standard privacy profile.
AI.result: The authors tabulate μ values for a wide useful range of parameters, and find that μ≈ε/5 is a conservative conversion that works well for general-purpose use cases.
AI.conclusion: The proposed principled conversion and the recommendation μ≈ε/5 provides practical guidance for practitioners to report privacy guarantees when switching from pure-DP to Gaussian differential privacy in privacy-preserving machine learning.

title: Generalized Rank-based Evaluation for Knowledge Graph Completion: Perspectives, Framework, and Analyses
summary: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) aims to predict missing facts from an observed knowledge graph (KG), playing a crucial role in a wide range of real-world applications such as drug discovery, recommender systems, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Although numerous KGC models have been proposed, the evaluation of KGC remains underexplored, despite its critical role in reliably assessing model performance and selecting appropriate models for real-world applications. In this paper, we introduce two important perspectives for KGC evaluation that are overlooked by existing evaluation metrics, (P1) predictive sharpness and (P2) popularity-bias robustness. To address both perspectives, we propose a generalized evaluation framework, PROBE, which consists of a rank transformer (RT) that estimates the score of each prediction based on a desired level of predictive sharpness and a rank aggregator (RA) that determines the final evaluation score by aggregating all prediction scores according to a desired level of popularity-bias robustness. We theoretically analyze PROBE by defining six key properties for reliable KGC evaluation and prove that PROBE satisfies all the properties, while existing metrics fail to satisfy some. In particular, due to the open-world nature of KGs, an evaluation metric should preserve the relative performance of KGC models even when only incomplete facts are observed. We show that PROBE better maintains such consistency, providing a more reliable estimate of intrinsic model performance than existing metrics. Extensive experiments with six KGC models on six real-world KGs reveal that existing metrics may over- or under-estimate model performance depending on different evaluation perspectives, whereas PROBE enables a more comprehensive, flexible, and consistent evaluation of KGC models.
